shippingNews.postTitle: Cleveland Welcomes Final Cruise Ship of Record-breaking 2026 Season

stories.body: Victory 1 at Cleveland in 2020. [Roger LeLievre] CLEVELAND, OH – The Port of Cleveland is set to welcome its final cruise ship of the 2026 season Sunday as the Victory I arrives at the docks and caps a record-setting year for Great Lakes cruising. The arrival will mark the port’s 54th vessel call of the season, surpassing the previous record of 53 calls set in 2025. It is the second consecutive year Cleveland has set a new record for cruise ship visits. The cruise season, which ran from April through October, brought more than 9,500 passengers to Northeast Ohio, according to the Port of Clevel

shippingNews.postTitle: An Early-morning Visit from the Sam Laud

stories.body: At daybreak Sunday, Oct. 25, the Sam Laud was making her way out of Ludington, MI. Her broad black hull and rust-streaked white bow stood against a soft October sky, with two crew members visible near the forecastle. After a brief visit to unload stone, the veteran Great Lakes freighter was headed south again. The Sam Laud arrived in Ludington at about 4 a.m. from the Drummond Island Quarry in northern Lake Huron. todayInHistory.title: Sam Laud
todayInHistory.text: Sam Laud Bay Shipbuilding Corp. of Sturgeon Bay, WI, laid the keel for their hull # 712 on Jan. 4, 1974 to be built as a smaller-sized Great Lakes self-unloading bulk cargo carrier. The new vessel was launched on Nov. 19, 1974 for Buffalo's American Steamship Co. (ASC), a subsidiary of GATX Corp., Chicago, IL. Completed in 1975, the self-unloader was christened Sam Laud by Mrs. Edna Laud on behalf of her husband at a christening ceremony held April 15, 1975. Mr. Laud was the former president (1945) and chairman of the board (1956) of GATX Corp., having started with the company in 1916 as shop painter and riveter. Mr. Laud died August 1, 1963. GATX Corp. had acquired ASC in July of 1973. Mrs. Laud was accompanied by Mr. Frederick G. Jaicks, chairman and CEO of Inland Steel Co., Chicago, IL, who gave the address at the christening ceremonies. One of a new generation of self-unloaders for the ASC fleet, the Sam Laud was built at an approximate cost of $13.3 million and was the fourth of 10 self-unloaders launched for the fleet under Chapter XI of the Merchant Marine Act of 1970. Under this act, the U.S. government-guaranteed financing and tax deferred benefits for fleet modernizing. The other ASC self-unloaders built under this program were the Roger M. Kyes (now Adam E. Cornelius, 1973), Charles E. Wilson (now John J. Boland, 1973), H. Lee White (1974), St. Clair (1976), Belle River (now Walter J. marineWeather.synopsis: 30.5 inch high pressure centered over northern Ontario this morning shifts east to the Saint Lawrence Seaway this evening, with 30.4 inch ridging over Lake Superior weakening to 30.1 inches through tonight. A developing 29.8 inch Colorado low lifts through the Plains on Wednesday, eventually moving across Lake Superior Wednesday night into early Thursday morning. High pressure of 30.2 to 30.3 inches returns to the Upper Great Lakes by Friday, strengthening to 30.4 inches over the Lower Great Lakes on Saturday as ridging of 30.1 to 30.2 inches lingers over Lake Superior through the weekend.

A large area of high pressure around 30.5 inches will slowly track from Ontario into New England through today into tomorrow morning, while weakening low pressure will move northward across Minnesota into Canada. Modest to breezy southeast winds from 15 to 20 knots today and evening will shift south late tonight through Wednesday. Some gust to 25 knots may occur tonight over the northern third of Lake Michigan. Moderate southerlies then continue on Wednesday. A cold front will then gradually move across the lake on Thursday, with winds shifting from modest to breezy southwest winds Wednesday night to lighter northwest winds after the passage by Thursday afternoon.

High pressure, 30.50 inches, will settle over southern Quebec this evening. Low pressure is forecast to move across northern Ontario into Quebec on Thursday, dragging a cold front across the Great Lakes. This front will provide the next chance for light rain.

High pressure of 30.50 inches will strengthen over the eastern Great Lakes today before moving off the New England Coast Wednesday. The next cold front slides south across Lake Erie Thursday night. High pressure of 30.40 inches will build over the eastern Great Lakes again Friday into Saturday.

A ridge averaging 30.6 inches affects the lake through Thursday as the embedded high pressure center wobbles southeastward from northern Ontario to North Atlantic waters southeast of the Canadian Maritimes. The ridge exits eastward Thursday night as a cold front sweeps eastward across the lake. Behind the front, another ridge averaging 30.2 inches builds from the western Great Lakes through this Saturday.
